body:
Complete guide to Pokémon Unite. Learn about the best Pokémon to use, tier lists, held items, and strategies for winning ranked matches in Pokémon Unite.

Pokémon Unite is a free-to-play MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) featuring Pokémon characters. With its fast-paced gameplay and strategic depth, it has become a popular competitive game. This guide covers everything you need to know to succeed in Pokémon Unite, from basic mechanics to advanced strategies.

Table of Contents

  1. Game Basics
  2. Pokémon Roles
  3. Best Pokémon to Use
  4. Held Items
  5. Map Strategy
  6. Ranked Tips
  7. Conclusion

Game Basics

Pokémon Unite is a 5v5 MOBA where two teams compete to score the most points within 10 minutes. Players control Pokémon characters, defeat wild Pokémon for experience and Aeos Energy, and score the energy in the opponent goal zones. The team with the most points at the end wins.

The map features two lanes (top and bottom) and a central jungle area. Each lane has goal zones where players can score points. The central jungle contains powerful wild Pokémon that give significant experience and buffs when defeated.

The game is divided into phases. In the early game, players focus on leveling up and defeating wild Pokémon. In the mid game, players start team fights and contest objectives. In the late game, the most powerful wild Pokémon (Zapdos, Rotom, and Regieleki) spawn, providing massive advantages to the team that defeats them.

Pokémon Roles

Each Pokémon in Unite falls into one of five roles: Attacker, Defender, Speedster, Supporter, and All-Rounder. Understanding these roles is essential for building a balanced team.

Attackers are ranged Pokémon that deal high damage but have low HP. They include Pikachu, Cinderace, and Gardevoir. Attackers should stay behind their team and deal damage from a safe distance. Positioning is critical for attackers, as they are easily killed if caught out.

Defenders are tanky Pokémon that protect their team and control areas. They include Snorlax, Slowbro, and Crustle. Defenders should engage the enemy team first, soak up damage, and protect their attackers. Defenders are essential for team fights.

Speedsters are melee Pokémon that excel at jungle clearing and burst damage. They include Gengar, Zeraora, and Absol. Speedsters are fragile but can deal massive damage to isolated targets. They should roam the jungle and gank lanes to get kills.

Supporters provide utility through healing, shielding, and crowd control. They include Blissey, Mr. Mime, and Eldegoss. Supporters should stay with their team and provide assistance in team fights. They are essential for keeping attackers alive.

All-Rounders are melee Pokémon that balance offense and defense. They include Lucario, Charizard, and Machamp. All-Rounders can engage fights, deal damage, and survive. They are versatile and can fill multiple roles on a team.

Best Pokémon to Use

The Pokémon Unite meta changes with each patch, but some Pokémon consistently perform well. Here are the top Pokémon to use in each role:

Top Attackers: Cinderace, Gardevoir, and Pikachu are consistently strong attackers. Cinderace has high mobility and damage, Gardevoir has powerful area-of-effect moves, and Pikachu has excellent crowd control.

Top Defenders: Snorlax, Slowbro, and Trevenant are top-tier defenders. Snorlax has incredible bulk and crowd control, Slowbro has excellent sustain, and Trevenant has unique mechanics that make it difficult to kill.

Top Speedsters: Gengar, Absol, and Dodrio are strong speedsters. Gengar has powerful burst damage, Absol has high mobility and critical hits, and Dodrio has incredible speed and area-of-effect damage.

Top Supporters: Blissey, Clefable, and Mr. Mime are top supporters. Blissey provides healing and shielding, Clefable has unique gravity mechanics, and Mr. Mime has excellent crowd control.

Top All-Rounders: Lucario, Machamp, and Tsareena are strong all-rounders. Lucario has excellent mobility and damage, Machamp has powerful crowd control, and Tsareena has high sustain and area-of-effect damage.

Held Items

Held items are essential for maximizing your Pokémon potential. Each Pokémon can hold up to three items, and upgrading them to level 30 is crucial for competitive play. Here are the best items to use:

Buddy Barrier: Gives a shield when using your Unite Move. This item is essential for almost every Pokémon, as it provides survivability during team fights. Maximize this item first.

Focus Band: Provides passive healing when HP is low. This item is excellent for defenders and all-rounders that need to survive extended fights. Upgrade this for tanky Pokémon.

Muscle Band: Increases basic attack damage based on the target HP. This item is excellent for attackers and all-rounders that rely on basic attacks. Upgrade this for physical attackers.

Shell Bell: Reduces move cooldowns when landing moves. This item is excellent for special attackers that rely on moves rather than basic attacks. Upgrade this for special attackers.

Score Shield: Provides a shield when scoring, preventing interruption. This item is essential for scoring in difficult situations. Upgrade this for Pokémon that need to score in contested areas.

Map Strategy

Map awareness is critical in Pokémon Unite. Here are some key strategies for each phase of the game:

Early Game (0:00-7:00): Focus on leveling up and clearing wild Pokémon. The jungle (Speedster) should clear the central camp quickly, while the laners should defeat the wild Pokémon in their lanes. Do not engage in team fights until you have reached at least level 5.

Mid Game (7:00-2:00): Start contesting objectives. The first Drednaw spawn is critical, as it provides a shield to the entire team. If you win the Drednaw fight, push your advantage by scoring and taking Rotom. If you lose, play defensively and wait for the next objective.

Late Game (2:00-0:00): The final two minutes are the most important. Points are doubled, and Zapdos (or Rayquaza in some maps) spawns. Defeating Zapdos makes all goal zones vulnerable to instant scoring. If your team defeats Zapdos, push all lanes and score as much as possible. If the enemy defeats Zapdos, defend your goal zones at all costs.

Ranked Tips

Climbing the ranked ladder requires more than just good mechanics. Here are some tips for climbing efficiently:

  • Master one or two Pokémon: Do not try to learn every Pokémon. Focus on mastering one or two in your preferred role.
  • Upgrade your held items: Item level makes a huge difference. Focus on upgrading essential items like Buddy Barrier and Focus Band.
  • Communicate with your team: Use the quick chat feature to coordinate objectives and ganks.
  • Watch the minimap: Map awareness is critical. Always know where the enemy team is.
  • Do not overextend: Do not push too far without vision or backup. It is better to play safe and score later.
  • Focus on objectives: Kills do not win games — scoring does. Prioritize objectives over kills.
  • Stay positive: Tilt is your worst enemy. If you lose several games in a row, take a break.

Conclusion

Pokémon Unite is a complex and rewarding MOBA that requires both mechanical skill and strategic thinking. By understanding roles, mastering Pokémon, upgrading items, and executing map strategies, you can climb the ranked ladder and become a top player.
